title: 179. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Factoring Cubic Differences and Sums
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial of the form \(a^3+b^3\) using the sum of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3+8\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(x^3+8\) as a sum of cubes, then use the identity \(a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)\) with \(a=x\) and \(b=2\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^3+8 &= x^3+2^3\\
&= (x+2)(x^2-2x+4)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x+2)(x^2-2x+4)\).
questions.hint: Use the sum of cubes identity \(a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)\).

questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial of the form \(a^3-b^3\) using the difference of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3-27\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(x^3-27\) as a difference of cubes, then use \(a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)\) with \(a=x\) and \(b=3\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^3-27 &= x^3-3^3\\
&= (x-3)(x^2+3x+9)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x-3)(x^2+3x+9)\).
questions.hint: Use the difference of cubes identity \(a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Sum of Cubes with a Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Factor an expression of the form \((ax)^3+b^3\) using the sum of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(8x^3+1\).
questions.explanation:
Recognize the sum of cubes, then use \(a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)\) with \(a=2x\) and \(b=1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
8x^3+1 &= (2x)^3+1^3\\
&= (2x+1)(4x^2-2x+1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((2x+1)(4x^2-2x+1)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Difference of Cubes with a Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Factor an expression of the form \((ax)^3-b^3\) using the difference of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(27x^3-64\).
questions.explanation:
Write the expression as a difference of cubes, then use \(a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)\) with \(a=3x\) and \(b=4\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
27x^3-64 &= (3x)^3-4^3\\
&= (3x-4)(9x^2+12x+16)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((3x-4)(9x^2+12x+16)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Sum of Cubes with a Sixth-Power Term
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^6+1\) by treating it as a sum of cubes.
questions.question: Factor \(x^6+1\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(x^6+1\) as a sum of cubes, then use \(a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)\) with \(a=x^2\) and \(b=1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^6+1 &= (x^2)^3+1^3\\
&= (x^2+1)(x^4-x^2+1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x^2+1)(x^4-x^2+1)\).
questions.hint: Treat \(x^6\) as \((x^2)^3\) before applying the sum of cubes identity.

questions.concept: Factoring a Sum of Cubes with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(8a^3+27b^3\) using the sum of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(8a^3+27b^3\).
questions.explanation:
Recognize the sum of cubes, then use \(u^3+v^3=(u+v)(u^2-uv+v^2)\) with \(u=2a\) and \(v=3b\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
8a^3+27b^3 &= (2a)^3+(3b)^3\\
&= (2a+3b)(4a^2-6ab+9b^2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((2a+3b)(4a^2-6ab+9b^2)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Difference of Cubes with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(125x^3-8y^3\) using the difference of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(125x^3-8y^3\).
questions.explanation:
Write the expression as a difference of cubes, then use \(a^3-b^3=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)\) with \(a=5x\) and \(b=2y\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
125x^3-8y^3 &= (5x)^3-(2y)^3\\
&= (5x-2y)(25x^2+10xy+4y^2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((5x-2y)(25x^2+10xy+4y^2)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Sum of Cubes with Larger Coefficients
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(64a^3+125b^3\) using the sum of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(64a^3+125b^3\).
questions.explanation:
Recognize the sum of cubes, then use \(u^3+v^3=(u+v)(u^2-uv+v^2)\) with \(u=4a\) and \(v=5b\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
64a^3+125b^3 &= (4a)^3+(5b)^3\\
&= (4a+5b)(16a^2-20ab+25b^2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((4a+5b)(16a^2-20ab+25b^2)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Sum of Cubes with a Power of a Variable
questions.learningObjective: Factor \(x^3y^6+8\) using the sum of cubes identity.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3y^6+8\).
questions.explanation:
Write the expression as a sum of cubes, then use \(a^3+b^3=(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)\) with \(a=xy^2\) and \(b=2\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^3y^6+8 &= (xy^2)^3+2^3\\
&= (xy^2+2)(x^2y^4-2xy^2+4)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((xy^2+2)(x^2y^4-2xy^2+4)\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Difference of Cubes After Removing a Common Monomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a polynomial completely by removing a common monomial and then factoring a difference of cubes.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^4-16x\) completely.
questions.explanation:
First factor out the common monomial \(2x\), then factor \(x^3-8\) as a difference of cubes. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x^4-16x &= 2x(x^3-8)\\
x^3-8 &= x^3-2^3\\
&= (x-2)(x^2+2x+4)\\
2x^4-16x &= 2x(x-2)(x^2+2x+4)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the complete factorization is \(2x(x-2)(x^2+2x+4)\).
questions.hint: Remove the common monomial first, then apply the difference of cubes identity.
